title: Continuity and Change in a Community Library: A Simulated Lecture
instructions: 本材料为模拟教学练习，不是官方雅思试题，也不代表任何官方分数。请先听/读英文讲座稿（transcript），再完成10道听力理解题。题目类型包括单选、填空、匹配（用单选形式）和判断正误/未提及（True/False/Not Given，三选一）。填空答案必须来自原文，且不超过字数限制。之后学习语法讲解（中文），完成8道新句子的语法题。最后进行口语和写作迁移练习。所有题目和选项均为英文，解释为中文。
transcript:
Good evening, everyone. Thank you for coming to this public lecture. My name is Dr. Helen Marsh, and I work in the Department of Urban Studies. Tonight I want to talk about a small but revealing case: the Northside Community Library. I will analyse how an institution can change while keeping its core identity. Please feel free to take notes, and I will take questions at the end.

Let me start with a question. When does an institution truly change? Is it when the building is renovated, when the staff are replaced, or when the daily routines shift? I will argue that real change happens when the relationship between the institution and its users is renegotiated. The Northside Library is a good example because it has survived three major transitions in forty years.

First, some background. The library opened in 1982 in a former post office. For its first decade, it mainly lent books and provided quiet reading rooms. The users were mostly older residents and schoolchildren. The staff knew many readers by name. This personal knowledge was the library's greatest asset, and it shaped everything the library did.

In the 1990s, the local economy changed. Many young families moved into the area, and they asked for different services: evening opening hours, children's story sessions, and computer access. The library responded by extending its hours and creating a small computer corner. Notice that the building did not change much, but the institution did. The staff had to learn new skills, and the users began to see the library as a community hub rather than only a book lender.

Then, in the 2000s, a financial crisis hit the city budget. The library faced a 30 percent cut. The director at the time, Mr. Alvarez, made a controversial decision: he reduced the book budget and invested in partnerships with local schools and charities. Some residents protested. They said the library was abandoning its core mission. Mr. Alvarez argued that the library was protecting its core mission by finding new ways to serve people. This debate is important because it shows that continuity and change are not opposites; they are often two sides of the same decision.

Finally, in the 2010s, the library underwent a digital transformation. It introduced online catalogues, e-book lending, and a small makerspace with 3D printers. Interestingly, the physical visits did not decline as some had predicted. Instead, visits increased by 15 percent, especially among teenagers. Why? Because the makerspace gave young people a reason to come together. The library had become a place for collaboration, not just consumption.

So what can we learn from this case? I want to highlight three lessons. First, institutions survive by adapting their services, not by freezing their routines. Second, the users' sense of ownership matters more than the building itself. Third, leaders must explain change clearly, because people need to see how the past connects to the future.

Let me add one caution. Not all change is good. The library also tried a subscription model for premium services in 2015, and it failed. Users saw it as unfair. The library cancelled the scheme after six months. This failure is as instructive as the successes. It shows that change must respect the institution's values.

In conclusion, the Northside Library did not stay the same, and it did not become something entirely different. It changed its services while preserving its purpose: to support learning and connection. That, I suggest, is the real meaning of institutional continuity. Thank you. I am happy to take your questions now.

answers: Real change happens when the relationship between the institution and its users is renegotiated.

grammar.title: 指代、词性与平行结构；长句拆解
grammar.explanation: 在英语长句中，代词（如 it, they, this, that）用来指代前文出现的人或事物，使句子连贯。词性（名词、动词、形容词、副词）决定词在句中的功能。平行结构指用相同的语法形式连接并列成分，如动词与动词并列、名词与名词并列。拆解长句时，先找主句的主语和谓语，再分析从句和修饰成分。例如：'It changed its services while preserving its purpose' 中，It 指代 the library，changed 是谓语，while preserving 是状语。
grammar.example: It changed its services while preserving its purpose: to support learning and connection.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct pronoun: The library extended its hours, and ______ created a computer corner.
questions.explanation: The library 是单数机构，用 it 指代。

questions.prompt: Choose the correct word form: The staff had to learn new ______.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct parallel structure: The library introduced online catalogues, e-book lending, and ______.

questions.evidence: It introduced online catalogues, e-book lending, and a small makerspace with 3D printers.

questions.evidence: Some residents protested. They said the library was abandoning its core mission.

questions.evidence: Third, leaders must explain change clearly, because people need to see how the past connects to the future.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct parallel structure: The library did not stay the same, and it did not ______ something entirely different.
questions.explanation: did not 后接动词原形，与 stay 平行。
questions.evidence: In conclusion, the Northside Library did not stay the same, and it did not become something entirely different.

answers: The debate about the library's mission

questions.evidence: Mr. Alvarez argued that the library was protecting its core mission by finding new ways to serve people. This debate is important because it shows that continuity and change are not opposites; they are often two sides of the same decision.

questions.evidence: The library cancelled the scheme after six months.
